items.headline: Microsoft Patch Tuesday: 974 CVEs including two actively exploited zero-days
bullets: Microsoft released fixes for 974 vulnerabilities in September 2026 Patch Tuesday, including CVE-2026-81963 (Windows Update Stack privilege escalation) and CVE-2026-85880 (Advanced Local Procedure Call elevation of privilege), both under active exploitation.
Both zero-days allow low-privileged local attackers to escalate to SYSTEM-level access; attackers use these to gain full administrative control and are actively exploiting them in the wild.

This represents a significant vulnerability load alongside GitLab's critical path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-85706) being actively exploited, expanding the attack surface across infrastructure tooling.
items.source: Check Point Research Threat Intelligence Report, September 14 2026 & Cybersecurity Dive
items.novelty: Two new actively exploited zero-days in Windows kernel components, distinct from the previously reported ShieldCrash Defender bypass pattern.

items.headline: GitLab CVE-2026-85706 critical path traversal flaw now under active exploitation
bullets: CISA added CVE-2026-85706 (GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; the flaw permits unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files through repository commits API without authentication.
GitLab patched the vulnerability on September 10; CISA listed it on September 14 after malicious actors began exploiting it; maximum CVSS score of 10.0 across affected versions 18.7 through 19.3.1.
Federal agencies must mitigate by Monday per CISA mandate; demonstrates supply-chain risk as many development teams rely on GitLab for CI/CD and repository management.
items.source: Cybersecurity Dive, CISA; Senserva CVE tracker
items.novelty: Now actively exploited in the wild, moving from disclosed vulnerability to confirmed weaponization within days of patch availability.

items.headline: Multiple third-party infrastructure flaws joining active exploitation wave
bullets: Chromium V8 type confusion (CVE-2026-85046) and out-of-bounds write (CVE-2026-87491) plus multiple MikroTik RouterOS critical flaws and Citrix NetScaler issues now confirmed exploited; JFrog Artifactory authentication bypass vulnerabilities exploited for backdoor deployment.
ConnectWise ScreenConnect flaw allowing file upload and execution without authorization; D-Link and Totolink router firmware RCE flaws (CVSS 9.9–9.8) dominating hardware attack surface.
Pattern indicates coordinated exploitation across management interfaces and remote access tools, increasing risk for distributed infrastructure and branch office deployments.
items.source: Senserva Trustworthy AI CVE Ranking, CVE Brief, Check Point Research
items.novelty: Breadth of simultaneous exploitation across governance, CI/CD, networking, and remote access layers beyond traditional application flaws—systems engineer concern.

items.headline: BlueMoon exploit chain: Chromium V8 + Windows kernel escalation in active campaigns
bullets: Security researchers detailed BlueMoon, combining V8 JavaScript type confusion (CVE-2026-85046) with Windows privilege escalation to escape browser sandbox and gain kernel-level access on targeted systems.
Espionage groups deployed this against targets after Chrome patches became available, exploiting the lag time before patches reach vulnerable browser instances.
Demonstrates end-to-end browser-to-kernel compromise path: attackers need only web visit to compromise Windows machine; impacts any unpatched Chromium derivative.
items.source: Check Point Research Threat Intelligence Report
items.novelty: Multi-layer exploit chain linking browser JavaScript confusion with Windows kernel escalation—distinct attack pattern from typical sandbox escapes.

items.headline: Bay Area weather: Cooler with 60s coast, 70s bay, 80s inland; dry skies throughout
bullets: Monday features 60s on the coast, 70s along the bayshore, and highs near 80s inland with a mix of clouds and sun; skies will remain dry through the forecast.
Cooling trend continues from late last week when peak heat subsided 15-20 degrees; low-pressure system developing mid-week will reinforce cooler pattern.
A very slight chance of rain possible along coastal North Bay areas mid-week, but most of the week dry.
items.source: KRON4 SF Bay Area, Press Democrat, National Weather Service
items.novelty: Confirmation of seasonal transition out of multi-day heat wave into cooler, drier pattern.
